column2: A crane-game cabinet. The top row is the glass box's ceiling with the claw on its gantry; the bottom row is a pile of plush toys, and the four digits are plush numerals (soft, rounded, stitched, with button eyes) lying in the pile. A chute hole sits at one end. Idle: the claw creeps along the rail and sways, a coin rattles, the plushies settle and one blinks. Minute: the claw drops on the old digit, grabs, lifts it wobbling, and (comic suspense) carries it to the chute and drops it in; then a fresh plush is tossed in from above into the empty slot. Now and then the claw fumbles and has to retry. Hour: a jackpot, the claw grabs two at once, lights chase round the cabinet.

Lemmings. Little green-haired walkers stream in from a trapdoor at the top left and march across the glass, falling off edges, turning at walls. The digits are terrain built by them: builder lemmings lay bricks stair by stair, blockers stand with arms out, diggers tunnel down (custom terrain tiles). Idle: a steady stream walks over the digits, one shrugs, one parachutes down with an umbrella. Minute: a digger and a basher demolish the old digit and builders lay the new one brick by brick while the others walk across it. Hour: "Oh no!": a whole crowd explodes in little puffs and the exit door opens for the survivors.

A firefighter versus a blazing building. The digits are flames: each numeral is made of flickering fire tiles (the slow glass makes the flames lick and glow), rising from a window ledge. A firefighter in a helmet with a hose stands on the bottom row; the water arcs as ROM dots and splashes. Idle: the flames flicker and send up sparks, the firefighter adjusts the hose, wipes sweat, a cat waits on a ledge. Minute: he hoses down the old digit, which sizzles into smoke puffs, and the fire flares up again in the shape of the new digit. Hour: a fire engine rolls in, the ladder extends, and the cat is rescued.

A granny in a rocking chair knits the time. The digits are knitted fabric: custom tiles of knit stitches (little V chevrons), each numeral a knitted panel hanging from the needles, growing row by row. A ball of yarn sits on the floor and a kitten bats it. Idle: needles click (alternating poses every half second), the chair rocks, the yarn ball jiggles, the kitten pounces. Minute: the kitten pulls a loose thread and the old digit unravels row by row into a wavy yarn line, then granny knits the new digit up row by row. Hour: the kitten tangles everything and granny knits a whole new scarf.

A pinball table turned sideways on the 16x2 glass. The flippers sit at the right end, the ball rolls and bounces across the glass (the slow glass smear is its trail), and the four digits are lit bumpers and drop-targets: each numeral is a bank of targets that light when hit. Idle: the ball bounces between bumpers, the flippers flick it back, a bumper flashes on each hit, the score clicks up. Minute: the ball smashes the old digit's targets, they drop flat, and the new digit's targets pop up and light. Hour: multiball, TILT almost, a jackpot flash, and a replay knock.

A bored office clerk with a rubber stamp. The digits are stamped ink impressions on paper slips (custom tiles with a slightly blotchy, imperfect ink texture and a stamp border), lined up on the desk; an in-tray and an out-tray sit at the ends; the clerk sits behind the desk with a mug. Idle: he sips coffee, yawns, drums his fingers, inks the stamp on the pad, glances at a wall clock. Minute: he pulls the old slip into the out-tray, slides a fresh slip in, and THUNK stamps the new digit (the slow glass gives the ink a soft bleed), with a little bounce of the desk. Hour: an avalanche of paperwork from the in-tray and a frenzied stamping spree.
